name: JustRigIt – local video mocap + auto-rig for game engines
summary: Free, open-source tool that turns a phone video into game-ready character animation on your own PC: NVIDIA GEM-X tracks body, fingers and root motion locally, then JustRigIt cleans it up (floor, facing, smoothing, foot locking), auto-rigs your GLB/GLTF/FBX character and exports for Unreal 5, Godot 4, Unity or Blender with engine-specific bone names. No account, no upload.

access.notes: App is AGPL (modified versions offered as a service must share source). Capture installer downloads GEM-X weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License (commercial use allowed). Video capture: Windows 10/11 + NVIDIA RTX 8 GB+ VRAM; no GitHub release published yet.

procedure: Download the repo ZIP from https://github.com/SuddleMercury/justrigit (no release build is published yet).
Open Start-JustRigIt.bat (or dist/justrigit.html in a modern browser) for rigging, retargeting and export.
For video capture on Windows with an NVIDIA RTX GPU, run Install-Capture.bat once (~15 GB: Python, PyTorch, ffmpeg, GEM-X model).
Drop a phone video (whole body, up to 60 s), pick the mannequin or your own GLB/GLTF/FBX character.
Choose Unreal 5, Godot 4, Unity or Blender and in-place or root motion, then download the zip with the import guide.

stats.size: app 1 MB HTML; capture install ~15 GB

verdict.why: Useful local mocap-to-engine pipeline built on commercially usable GEM-X weights, with clear third-party license notes. Single-author project (2 stars, no release, last commit 11-03), Windows/RTX-only capture; I could not run the capture on the box.
